value.text:
October 9, 2026 Decision 30958-D01-2026

Kneehill Solar GP Inc.
2930, 155 Wellington Street West
Toronto, Ont. M5V 3H1

Attention: Yasser Beshr

Kneehill Energy Storage Facility Letter of Enquiry
Proceeding 30958
Application 30958-A001

Approval of minor amendments

1. Kneehill Solar GP Inc., by Application 30958-A001, registered on July 21, 2026, applied
to the Alberta Utilities Commission for approval to make minor amendments to the 10-megawatt
(MW) energy storage facility within the existing Kneehill Solar Generation Facility boundary, in
the Three Hills area.

2. The proposed work is related to facilities previously approved by the Commission but not
yet constructed in Approval 30539-D02-2026.
1

3. Kneehill Solar requested to update the equipment of the battery energy storage system
from the SolBank system to the HyperBlock system, a type of HyperStrong system.
Kneehill Solar indicated that the number of containers would be reduced from eight to five,
inverters would be reduced from eight to three, and transformers would be reduced from four to
three. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the HyperBlock system uses the same lithium iron
phosphate battery chemistry as the approved configuration and that the proposed changes are not
changing the battery technology or associated characteristics.
2

4. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the project capability remains the same as what was
approved, at 10 MW/20 megawatt-hours.

5. Kneehill Solar stated that the proposed HyperBlock system incorporates safety systems
and design features that are comparable to the approved SolBank system and are intended to
prevent, detect and mitigate thermal events, fire hazards and explosion risks. Kneehill Solar
confirmed that it will continue to meet the safety obligations in the approval, including energy
storage facility-related training, ongoing safety upgrades and annual updates to the site-specific
emergency response plan.

1
 Energy Storage Facility Approval 30539-D02-2026, Proceeding 30539, Application 30539-A001,
January 28, 2026.
2
 Exhibit 30958-X0001, Letter of Enquiry for Minor Amendment, PDF page 2. Alberta Utilities Commission
October 9, 2026  Page 2 of 2

6. Kneehill Solar provided a letter from Stantec Consulting Ltd., which confirmed that the
original dispersion modelling and risk assessment prepared by Calvin Consulting Group Ltd. for
the approved battery system remains valid and that the carbon monoxide release rates observed
during HyperBlock testing are below the carbon monoxide emission rate used in the original
modelling assessment.
3
 Kneehill Solar confirmed that the proposed HyperBlock system would
not be expected to result in materially different hydrogen fluoride emissions or hydrogen
fluoride-related risk outcomes than the system evaluated in the original assessment.
4

7. Kneehill Solar retained Green Cat Renewables Canada Corporation to complete a noise
impact assessment for the proposed equipment which concluded that the project will comply
with Rule 012: Noise Control.
5

8. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the proposed changes are limited to internal equipment
arrangement to be located within the approved project boundary.

9. Kneehill Solar has provided information respecting the need, nature, extent, land
affected, land ownership and the timing of the work. Kneehill Solar also stated that no adverse
environmental impact will be caused by the proposed work.

10. Based upon the information provided, the Commission is satisfied that the proposed
amendment to the energy storage facility is of a minor nature, no person is directly and adversely
affected by the proposal, and no significant adverse environmental impact will be caused by the
proposed work. The Commission approves the amendment to the energy storage facility.

11. Approval 30958-D02-2026 is attached.

12. The Commission may, no later than 60 days from the date of this decision and without
notice, correct typographical, spelling and calculation errors and other similar types of errors and
post the corrected decision on its website.

Alberta Utilities Commission

Rita Chan
Director – Power Plants, Facilities Division
On behalf of the Alberta Utilities Commission

Attachment

3
 Exhibit 30958-X0012, KneehillSolar-Response_to_AUC_Information_Request_Round_1.
4
 Exhibit 30958-X0018, KneehillSolar-Response_to_AUC_Information_Request_Round_2.
5
 Exhibit 30958-X0015, Attachment 3 - Kneehill BESS - LOE NIA Letter.

Proceeding 30732 Register
Application 30732-A001
Decision 30732-D01-2026
AUC contact: Victor Choy
403-592-4439 or victor.choy@auc.ab.ca
Synapse Real Estate Corp: Jason Van Gaal
613-797-3311 or jason@synapsedatacenter.com
Overview
Synapse Real Estate Corp applied to construct and operate a combined-cycle natural gas-fired power plant with a nominal capacity of approximately 1,400 megawatts (MW) as well as 1,800 MW of emergency and backup diesel generation (the power plant). The application stated that the power plant will not be connected to the Alberta Interconnection Electric System but will be used to power the on-site data centre load. The application was filed under the Hydro and Electric Energy Act.
On August 17, 2026, the AUC denied the Synapse Data Center Power Plant Project application. The Commission finds that the project is too close to the surrounding community, and Synapse failed to demonstrate any compelling justification for selecting that location. The site is simply not suitable for the proposed development. In making this finding, the Commission is not commenting on the suitability of a data centre in this location. The Commission does not approve or regulate data centres.
Hearing information
To learn more about the review process, or for more information about how you may become involved in this proceeding, please contact us or visit the following webpages:
Review process for facility applications
Have your say about a utility project
Participate in an AUC hearing
The eFiling System​
The eFiling System should be accessed to view the applications and the other documents the AUC will be considering in this proceeding. The system is also used to file submissions and evidence to participate in the proceeding.
To create an account, select “New account” and follow the steps to create a user ID and password. If you have any questions about how to use the eFiling System please contact us at info@auc.ab.ca or 310-4AUC.
Documents being considered in this proceeding can be found in the eFiling​ System (which requires log in). Once you have logged in, enter 30732 in the “go to” section at the top left corner of your screen.
